summary: Led by the Spirit into the wilderness, Jesus fasts forty days and defeats the devil’s three temptations by answering each one with the word of God.
key_insight: All three of Jesus’ answers come from Deuteronomy 6–8, where Moses reminds Israel of its forty years of testing in the wilderness. Israel, called God’s son, failed there. Jesus, the Son, stands firm in His forty days.
story: Jesus, filled with the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan {Lk} and immediately the Spirit drove Him into the wilderness. He was there forty days, tempted by Satan, and was with the wild beasts. {Mk} In those days He ate nothing, and when they had ended, He was hungry. {Lk}

The tempter came to Him and said, “If You are the Son of God, command that these stones become bread.” Jesus answered, “It is written, ‘Man shall not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God.’ ” {Mt}

Then the devil took Him into the holy city, set Him on the pinnacle of the temple, and said, “If You are the Son of God, throw Yourself down.” He quoted Scripture too: God would give His angels charge over Him, and they would bear Him up, “Lest you dash your foot against a stone.” Jesus said to him, “It is written again, ‘You shall not tempt the LORD your God.’ ” {Mt}

Again, the devil took Him up on an exceedingly high mountain {Mt} and showed Him all the kingdoms of the world in a moment of time. {Lk} “All this authority I will give You, and their glory; for this has been delivered to me, and I give it to whomever I wish,” {Lk} he said, if only Jesus would fall down and worship him. Jesus said, “Away with you, Satan! For it is written, ‘You shall worship the LORD your God, and Him only you shall serve.’ ” {Mt}
When the devil had ended every temptation, he departed from Him until an opportune time. {Lk} And angels came and ministered to Him. {Mt}
differences: Matthew gives the order bread, temple, mountain; Luke gives bread, mountain, temple.
Mark tells it in two verses, does not describe the three temptations, and alone says Jesus “was with the wild beasts.”
Mark and Luke say Jesus was tempted during the forty days; Matthew and Luke describe three temptations that came when the forty days ended and He was hungry.
Luke alone records the devil’s claim that the world’s authority “has been delivered to me,” and says the devil left “until an opportune time.” Matthew and Mark say angels ministered to Jesus.
Jesus’ last rebuke is “Away with you, Satan!” in Matthew and “Get behind Me, Satan!” in Luke.

fit.question: Matthew puts the temple temptation second and the mountain third. Luke reverses them. Which order is right?

points.label: Matthew marks the sequence
points.text: In Greek, Matthew links the scenes with words that mark order (“then,” “again”), and his account ends naturally: Jesus commands, “Away with you, Satan!” and “Then the devil left Him.” Luke’s connecting words are simpler and do not insist on an order.

points.label: Luke ends in Jerusalem
points.text: Luke’s Gospel moves steadily toward Jerusalem and the temple (Luke 9:51), and it ends there. Placing the temple scene last gives the temptations a climax in Jerusalem. Many think Luke arranged the scenes this way on purpose.

fit.note: Matthew gives the sequence, and Luke arranges the same three temptations for emphasis without claiming a different order. Ancient writers could do this without error.
fit.short: Matthew’s Greek marks a sequence; Luke’s does not, and he arranges the scenes to end at the Jerusalem temple, a theme of his Gospel.

scene.label: The wilderness
scene.text: The Gospels do not name the place. It was probably the barren Judean wilderness between Jerusalem and the Jordan: bare hills, scorching days, cold nights, and few people. Mark’s “wild beasts” fit that empty land.

scene.label: Forty days
scene.text: Moses was with the Lord forty days and nights without bread (Exodus 34:28). Elijah traveled forty days and nights to Horeb (1 Kings 19:8). Israel spent forty years in the wilderness (Deuteronomy 8:2). Jesus’ forty days stand in that line.

scene.label: The pinnacle of the temple
scene.text: This was probably a high point on the temple walls, perhaps the southeast corner of the courts, which looked down a long drop into the Kidron Valley.

scene.label: The devil quotes a psalm
scene.text: Psalm 91:11–12 promises God’s protection to the one who trusts Him. The devil turned it into a dare. Jesus did not debate the psalm; He answered with another Scripture that showed how God’s promises are meant to be trusted, not tested.

witnesses.matthew: Ends with the mountain, where all the kingdoms are offered and refused. The King who will one day say, “All authority has been given to Me in heaven and on earth” (Matthew 28:18), will not take it from the devil’s hand.
witnesses.mark: Tells it in two verses with force: the Spirit “drove” Him out. Only Mark mentions the wild beasts, a picture of a lonely and dangerous place, where angels served Him.
witnesses.luke: Sets the temptation right after Jesus’ family line, which ends with “Adam, the son of God” (3:38). Where the first son of God fell, this Son stands. Luke ends at the temple and notes the devil left only “until an opportune time,” looking ahead to the Passion (22:3).

seeing.reveals: Jesus is the faithful Son who trusts His Father in hunger, refuses to force His Father’s hand, and will not take a crown on the devil’s terms.
seeing.living: Each temptation offered something good by the wrong road: bread, God’s protection, the kingdoms of the world. Jesus answered with Scripture He knew and obeyed, not with clever argument. Temptation is met the same way today, by trusting God’s word over the shortcut.
seeing.ponder: Where is the enemy offering you a shortcut to something God has promised to give in His own way and time?

preaching.big_idea: Where Israel failed in the wilderness, Jesus the Son stood firm on God’s word.
preaching.watch_for: The devil’s first words are “If You are the Son of God,” spoken right after the Father’s voice said, “This is My beloved Son” (3:17). The temptations test the very identity the baptism declared.

title: Jesus Is Tempted in the Wilderness
